An Address to Men of Science is a pamphlet by Richard Carlile, printed and published by the author at 55 Fleet Street, London, in 1821. It sold for one shilling. Britain, Carlile urges, should win the noble name of the land whence mankind shall be illuminated. The address also submits to their judgment a sketch of a proper system for the education of youth.

Carlile opens with a confession. He is not himself a man of experimental science, he says. All he knows has been acquired by reading. The pamphlet is a radical publisher's appeal, from a man who was repeatedly prosecuted for the books he sold. He asks the learned to do in public what he does from his shop: defend free inquiry against the church and the law.
podcast-tuckercarlson-GJe-8TyJhrw:
Teamsters president Sean O'Brien reveals to Tucker Carlson the words Kamala Harris left him with: I will win with or without you. The Teamsters famously declined to endorse a presidential candidate for the first time in decades. O'Brien's blunt hour explains the labor politics behind that break.

O'Brien describes his meetings with Harris and with Trump and how each treated the union. He argues Democrats took working voters for granted while offering little back. Carlson asks what the snub says about the party's future with labor. Working and political viewers get the union man's side of a famous last-words story.
